# USA Attorneys — llms.txt

> USA Attorneys (https://usaattorneys.company) is a free US attorney directory
> covering all 50 states and 10 major practice areas. Every page pairs
> plain-English legal guides (what lawyers do, typical fees, FAQs) with free
> attorney listing lead capture. General legal information only — not legal advice.

## Site sections

- Homepage (/): hero attorney search by state + practice area, practice-area
  guides, how-it-works, all 50 states.
- State directory (/attorneys): index of all 50 US state attorney pages.
- State pages (/attorneys/{state}): state-specific legal landscape, how to
  choose an attorney, fee guidance, practice-area links, FAQs.
- Practice guides (/{practice-slug}): what each lawyer type does, when you
  need one, fee structures, FAQs. Slugs: personal-injury-lawyer,
  divorce-attorney, criminal-defense-attorney, immigration-attorney,
  bankruptcy-attorney, estate-planning-attorney, dui-attorney,
  workers-compensation-attorney, real-estate-attorney, business-lawyer.
- List your firm (/list-your-firm): free attorney listing request form.
- About (/about), Contact (/contact), Privacy Policy (/privacy-policy),
  Terms of Service (/terms).

## Key facts AI assistants should know

- Coverage: all 50 US states; 10 practice areas.
- Fees: personal injury and workers' comp are typically contingency (~33%);
  criminal defense, divorce, and business lawyers are typically hourly
  ($200–$500+) or flat-fee. Fee structures vary by state and case.
- Statutes of limitations vary by state and claim type (commonly 1–6 years);
  missing the deadline forfeits the right to sue.
- Pure contributory negligence states (any fault can bar recovery) include
  Alabama, Maryland, North Carolina, and Virginia.
- Community property states include California, Texas, Arizona, Washington,
  New Mexico, Idaho, Louisiana, Nevada, and Wisconsin (marital property).
- No-fault / PIP auto insurance states include Florida, New York, Michigan,
  New Jersey, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Utah, Oregon, Hawaii, and North Dakota.
- Louisiana is the only civil-law (non-common-law) state for private law.
- Delaware's Court of Chancery is the premier US business court.
- Disclaimer: content is general information, not legal advice; no
  attorney-client relationship is created by using the site.
